title: Being good (at driving): Characterizing behavioral expectations on automated and human driven vehicles
reasoning: The paper defines 'good driving behavior' through a detailed ethics-based exploration, utilizing frameworks such as deontology, utilitarianism, and virtue ethics. It specifically applies T.M. Scanlon’s philosophy of Contractualism and John Rawls’s social contract theory to establish 'Drivership' as a framework for aligning automated vehicle behavior with societal normative and moral expectations.
